slides.title: Medical Affairs Must Own Its Value Story
bullets: The impact narrative is the structured, data-backed account of the function's value
It explains contributions to clinical decisions, evidence, and patient outcomes
Medical Affairs must define its own impact metrics and own that narrative
Rather than letting Commercial or Finance define success by default

slides.title: Combining Quantitative Data and Qualitative Cases
bullets: KPIs provide objectivity and comparability, but rarely tell the full story
A case where an MSL insight changed a study's design adds real context
A KOL testimonial about a collaboration makes the impact memorable

slides.title: Correlation Is Not Attribution
bullets: It's easy to show medical activity and good outcomes coexist in time
It's much harder to prove medical activity directly caused those outcomes
An honest narrative acknowledges that limit rather than overselling causality
The same discipline a rigorous MSL applies to clinical evidence

slides.title: A Value-Chain Narrative
bullets: Start from the activity performed, such as insights on an evidence gap
Show the strategic decision that activity informed, such as a new study
Close the loop with the documented outcome, when it can be shown

slides.title: Good Documentation Is the Raw Material
bullets: Contributing isn't extra work on top of the job
It's the natural extension of documenting insights and results well
Every well-documented field case can become the example that proves the value

takeaway.title: Medical Affairs proves its value by owning a disciplined, evidence-backed impact narrative
bullets: Quantitative KPIs and qualitative cases work together, not separately
A credible narrative distinguishes correlation from proven attribution
Well-documented field work is the raw material the whole narrative depends on
